Goal: Maximize lint pass rate across the codebase by iteratively applying automated fixes and targeted refactors, stopping only when the rate reaches the target threshold or the iteration budget is exhausted.
Scope: All source files tracked by the repository's configured linter (e.g., ESLint, Ruff, golangci-lint), excluding generated files and vendor directories.
Metric: lint_pass_rate — the ratio of lint-clean files to total linted files, expressed as a float in [0.0, 1.0] and measured by running the linter in check-only mode and parsing its exit code plus structured JSON output.
Verify: After each iteration, run `linter --format json` and compute pass_rate = (total_files - error_files) / total_files. Compare against the previous iteration's pass_rate. An iteration is accepted only if pass_rate >= previous_pass_rate (monotone non-regression). If pass_rate drops, roll back the iteration's changes and mark iteration as FAILED.
Guard: Invariant: lint_pass_rate must never decrease across accepted iterations. Implementation — before committing any fix batch, snapshot the current pass_rate; after applying fixes, re-measure; if new_rate < snapshot_rate, revert all changes in this batch via git restore and log a GUARD_VIOLATION event. Additionally, no iteration may introduce new lint rule categories not present in the baseline violation set (scope creep guard).

Iterations.early_stop_condition: lint_pass_rate >= 0.95 OR two consecutive iterations produce delta < 0.001
per_iteration_steps: 2. Run linter with --fix flag to apply auto-fixable violations
3. Re-run linter in check mode to compute new lint_pass_rate
4. Invariant guard check: if new_rate < snapshot_rate → revert + log GUARD_VIOLATION
5. If guard passes: commit fix batch with iteration index in message
6. Log iteration result: {iteration, snapshot_rate, new_rate, delta, status}
7. Check early-stop conditions; if met, exit loop and emit final report
